refuted_approach: CORRECTION AND RELABEL (session R0713, turn 5). (1) The sparsity and projection-stability entries are FORMALIZATIONS refuted, not directions. Enriched variants stay open: existential projection onto a coordinate subset; per-variable random restriction; sparsity combined with an oracle-gate-local condition. (2) Turn-4 inference corrected: Proposition R1 (spec ACC0-MOD6 p.15) states only that a reuse lemma valid for ALL functions needs c >= 1 (parity witness). It does NOT by itself say that a property satisfied by parity and IP is excluded. The correct step is: if a candidate P of MCSP[N^beta] holds for parity and IP, and the lemma derived from P would give c < 1 for the parity witness, the lemma would contradict R1. So P must fail on parity or IP, or the lemma must be MCSP-specific. This is a CONDITIONAL reduction, not a refutation by R1 alone. (3) Self-reducibility formalization (downward: f|_{x_m=0} is an instance of the same problem at threshold (N/2)^beta; random: f(x+r)+f(r) linear structure): parity satisfies both trivially (parity_m|_{x_m=0} = parity_{m-1}; parity is linear, so f(x)=f(x+r)+f(r)). IP satisfies the same kind of linear-in-one-argument identity on each block. So the formalization fails control (1) and is REFUTED as a standalone P. Enriched open variant: self-reducibility that is NOT inherited by restrictions (e.g. reduction to MCSP at a different threshold with an explicit size loss), tested on parity/IP.

refuted_approach: CANDIDATE P_r with polylog threshold (r*(f) <= (log s)^k for some fixed k) is REFUTED by control (1). Reasoning only, pending independent review. Parity_m: the B2 XOR block (u = a OR b, v = NAND(a,b), out = AND(u,v)) gives a chain of size 3(m-1) in which each block output has fan-out 2, so r = m-2. Schnorr (1976) states that 3(m-1) is the B2 circuit complexity of parity (SOURCE, not yet checked against the text), so the chain is size-minimal and r*(parity_m) <= m-2. With log s = beta*m and fixed k >= 2, m-2 <= (beta m)^2 for m >= 1/beta^2, so parity satisfies P_r. A property that parity satisfies cannot separate MCSP from parity, so by control (1) it cannot give c < 1.

Lemma (a): over B2 = {AND, OR, XOR} with free negation, parity_m (m>=2) has a circuit of m-1 gates in which every gate has fan-out 1 (left-deep XOR chain), so r*_B2(parity_m) = 0.
